Maria: heads-up — us-west GPU cluster has been saturated for ~6h, seen streaming p95 jump and non-stream queue explosion.
Maria: quick metric snapshot:
```
cluster: us-west
gpu_util: 96%
stream_p95: 420ms -> 720ms
nonstream_queue_len: 420
node_swap_events: 3
```
Maria: looks like admission wasn't enforcing streaming priority; non-stream jobs spilled into low-latency pools. Anyone else seeing this?
Ajay: yep I'm seeing the same in prometheus. autoscaler tagged a large rerank job as "general" and it got routed into realtime pools.
Ajay: admission-controller logs show many `accepted` for non-stream while streaming had backpressure. snippet of the log: `2026-03-18T09:12:03Z admit: job=rk-452 type=non-stream pool=rt-shared status=accepted`
Ajay: short-term: we can flip a policy to throttle non-stream and allow preemptions. example policy patch:
```yaml
admission_policy:
  name: prioritize_streaming
  type: rate_limit
  rules:
    - match: streaming
      max_rps: 200
      priority: high
    - match: non-stream
      max_rps: 20
      priority: low
  preempt: true
```
Leah: eu-west not affected (tracked separately). this is localized to us-west capacity. can we avoid hard preemptions that kill long batch tasks? soft preempt / graceful eviction would be better.
Carlos: we should also consider short-lived reserved capacity. spinning ephemeral spot-backed pool for 3-4 hours might flatten the queue. cost ballpark ~ $1.6k for 8 x A40-equivalent for 4h — cheaper than SLA-impact.
sre-bot: ALERT: cluster-gpu-saturation (us-west) — GPU util > 90% for 30m. https://grafana/redwood/alerts/12345
Maria: plan proposal (immediate):
1) apply rate-limit patch to admission-controller (non-stream -> 20rps).
2) create `us-west-rt-highprio` pool (8 GPUs) dedicated to streaming.
3) spin ephemeral spot pool to drain non-stream backlog.
Maria: I've drafted the curl to update the policy: 
```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  https://platform.internal/api/v1/admission/policies \
  -d '{"name":"prioritize_streaming","spec": {"rules":[{"match":"streaming","max_rps":200},{"match":"non-stream","max_rps":20}],"preempt":true}}'
```
Ajay: looks good. two caveats: preempt true needs `grace_period=120s` so checkpoints finish. also ensure `allow_fallback` so if highprio overflows, we still serve degraded results.
Ajay: YAML for pool creation (ops):
```yaml
pool: us-west-rt-highprio
replicas: 8
type: dedicated
labels: ["streaming","low-latency"]
autoscale: false
```
Leah: I'll kick off the spot pool and the policy change now. will set grace_period=120s. tagging this to `ops/billing` for cost approval.
Carlos: add charge code `infra:rt-temp` — I approve for up to $2k emergency spend.
Leah: running commands — uploading job logs if anything fails.
sre-bot: deploy: admission-policy/prioritize_streaming created by Leah at 2026-03-18T09:17:54Z
Leah: spot pool request submitted, 8 nodes requested, ETA ~5m.
Maria: monitoring — if streaming p95 doesn't drop below 250ms in 15m, we'll escalate to reserved capacity plan.
Ajay: note for follow-up: audit which job tags caused misrouting and add a stricter validation in the autoscaler tagging hook.
Carlos: also re-evaluate cost-vs-SLA: if this becomes frequent, we should pursue a small reserved slice for rt pools.
Leah: done — spot pool is up, admission policy in place. initial metrics look better (stream p95 -> 260ms, non-stream queue -> 180).
Maria: perfect. keep an eye on preempt evictions and requeue rates.
Carlos: thanks all.
Leah: thx :thumbsup:
